issues: The scene presents Nephi making an account on plates, a reasonable visual inference from his statement that he proceeds to give an account upon the plates, but the verse does not explicitly say he is writing at this moment.

Lettering must be an exact source quotation: '“he spake unto them concerning the Jews—”' is not verbatim in 1 Nephi 10:2, which reads 'For behold, it came to pass after my father had made an end of speaking the words of his dream, and also of exhorting them to all diligence, he spake unto them concerning the Jews—'
Lehi is shown speaking, but the verse reports what he said and does not specify whether he is speaking in this scene or describe any setting or audience.

Lettering must be an exact source quotation: '“Prepare ye the way of the Lord, and make his paths straight;”' is not verbatim in 1 Nephi 10:8, which reads 'Yea, even he should go forth and cry in the wilderness: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, and make his paths straight; for there standeth one among you whom ye know not; and he is mightier than I, whose shoe’s latchet I am not worthy to unloose. And much spake my father concerning this thing.'

Lehi is shown speaking, but the quoted passage reports what his father said; the scene does not establish that Lehi is speaking at this moment. The baptism is correctly treated as future, not a present event.

And after they had slain the Messiah, who should come, and after he had been slain he should rise from the dead, and should make himself manifest, by the Holy Ghost, unto the Gentiles.'

The tent and valley are supported, but the verse summarizes that the prior events occurred while Lehi dwelt there; it does not specify Lehi's actions or depict those events. The narration accurately quotes the verse.

Nephi is identified as narrator, but the verse does not specify that he is physically present in a scene; no visual setting or manifestation of the Holy Ghost is supported.
